title: The Last Blade 2
subtitle: A darker return
summary: The Last Blade 2 is SNK's weapon-based fighting sequel, first released for Neo Geo MVS in Japan on 25 November 1998.
body: The Last Blade 2 is SNK's weapon-based fighting sequel, first released for Neo Geo MVS in Japan on 25 November 1998. Returning fighters and newcomers continue the supernatural conflict within the late-Edo setting, presented with a darker mood and longer story sequences. The underlying system retains the Power and Speed styles of the first game, allowing the player to choose between heavier damage and connected attacks. Differences between the characters' strengths and weaknesses give that choice another context, encouraging a suitable approach for the fighter and opponent involved.

An additional EX mode combines elements of Power and Speed, extending the available ways to organise a character's offence. Deflection remains part of handling an incoming attack, so a sequence of strikes still carries the risk of being interrupted by a well-timed reply. The styles provide a framework, while distance and observation decide when an opportunity is safe to use. A familiar fighter can consequently feel different under another selection, with the same visual weapon supporting a different balance between a single damaging blow and a more elaborate exchange.

The presentation gives the final conflict more time through extended scenes and subdued colours, maintaining the series' attention to the setting around each duel. Neo Geo CD and later Dreamcast editions added material such as galleries and voiced scenes, while the original arcade game kept the fighting at the centre. The sequel's lasting appeal comes from that balance of atmosphere and precision. Its richly composed stages establish a place and a mood, then leave the players to resolve the encounter through movement, defensive timing and the chosen style's possibilities.
